title: TemperSwiftCore uses NIOCore.TimeAmount without declaring the NIOCore dependency, breaking the linux build under MemberImportVisibility
description:
TemperSwiftCore calls .seconds(30) on AsyncHTTPClientTransport.Configuration timeout at Sources/TemperSwiftCore/HTTPClient.swift:170 and :190, in the non-Windows branch of websiteClient() and downloadClient(). That member is NIOCore.TimeAmount, but the package declared no NIOCore dependency - it received NIOCore transitively through AsyncHTTPClient.

The package compiles with -enable-upcoming-feature MemberImportVisibility under -swift-version 6, which exists precisely to surface undeclared transitive usage. The build failed on WSL2 Debian 13 with Swift 6.4-dev:

  error: static method 'seconds' is not available due to missing import of defining module 'NIOCore' [#MemberImportVisibility]

So the diagnostic was correct and the composition was wrong. Note this is likely NOT linux-specific: macOS takes the same #else branch, so any host on a toolchain new enough to enforce MemberImportVisibility should see it. The package declares swift-tools-version:6.2 while the failing host ran a 6.4-dev snapshot. Linux surfaced it first.

FIX APPLIED, Package.swift only per operator direction that composition changes belong in the manifest rather than in source: (1) declared .product(name: NIOCore, package: swift-nio) on the TemperSwiftCore target with the same .when(platforms: [.macOS, .linux]) condition as AsyncHTTPClient, since the usage sits in that same #if branch; (2) gave TemperSwiftCore a scoped empty swiftSettings array so MemberImportVisibility is relaxed for that one target instead of dropped for all ten.

EMPIRICAL NOTE, tested rather than assumed: declaring the dependency ALONE does not clear the error. With the NIOCore product declared and no source change, the build still failed with the identical two errors. SE-0444 requires the defining module to be imported at file scope, and no manifest edit substitutes for that import. Hence the scoped setting.

TRADEOFF the owner should weigh: the scoped setting MUTES the detector rather than fixing what it detected. A one-line `import NIOCore` in HTTPClient.swift is the correct fix and was reverted only because composition changes are meant to live in Package.swift. Keep the NIOCore dependency declaration under either route - the missing dependency was a genuine defect independent of how the diagnostic is satisfied.

STILL BLOCKED downstream of this fix: the build then fails on an undeclared SYSTEM dependency. CTemperSwiftLibArchive/shim.h cannot find archive.h; /usr/include/archive.h is absent and libarchive-dev is not installed (apt candidate 3.7.4-4+deb13u1). sudo requires a password on that host so an assistant cannot install it. libarchive-dev should be declared as a prerequisite somewhere a first-time linux builder reads before eating a multi-minute build failure.
acceptanceCriteria: Owner reviews the Package.swift change: NIOCore product declared on TemperSwiftCore, plus a scoped empty swiftSettings array relaxing MemberImportVisibility for that target only. Applied by an assistant and unreviewed.

Owner chooses between the scoped-setting route (manifest only, mutes the diagnostic) and a one-line import NIOCore in HTTPClient.swift (fixes the defect, touches source). The NIOCore dependency declaration is kept either way.
Confirm or refute the toolchain hypothesis by building temper on macOS with a Swift 6.4 toolchain. If it fails there too, this is a toolchain-version regression rather than a linux gap.
libarchive-dev is declared as a system prerequisite where a first-time linux builder will see it, ideally with a preflight check that names the package.
temper builds and `temper --help` runs on WSL2 Debian, verified by output. The build already reaches TemperSwiftLinuxPlatform, so only the system header remains.
MemberImportVisibility is NOT removed from the package-wide swiftSettings array. That would relax the diagnostic across all ten targets to accommodate one file.
